title: Customer network emergency rollback & approval playbook (draft)
content:
Status: Draft
Owner: Aisha Patel (product-private-deployments)
Purpose: Capture emergency rollback and rapid-approval flows for customer-managed networking changes (VPC peering, route table updates, customer NAT changes) and define audit/logging requirements to ensure post-mortem and compliance coverage. This is deliberately operational: combination of PRD, runbook notes, and open questions.

1) Executive summary
- Problem: When customers manage their own network or when Redwood-managed control-plane changes affect customer routing, we occasionally need an emergency rollback or rapid approval to restore availability. Current docs focus on onboarding and approval gates; we lack a clear, auditable playbook for emergency rollback that spans customer-engineering, Redwood SRE, and security teams.
- Goal: Define a minimal set of approval gates, an auditable logging schema, and a fast execution path for rollbacks that preserves forensic evidence and meets enterprise compliance requirements.

2) Scope and non-goals
- In scope: customer-managed VPC handovers, on-premises gateway changes coordinated with Redwood Private, explicit rollback actions initiated by Redwood staff or customer ops, approval escalation sequences, and audit-log semantics for each action.
- Out of scope: low-risk UI changes to the Redwood Console (covered elsewhere), major re-architectures, and billing reconciliation.

3) Motivation and constraints
- Enterprise customers require an auditable trail for any emergency network action, including who granted approval, the exact rollback command or configuration, timestamps, and correlation to incident IDs.
- Time-to-restore SLO: 15–60 minutes depending on severity tier (see severity matrix below).
- Security/compliance: All approval gates must be recorded in the control plane and mirrored to customer-provided logging endpoints when configured (S3, Splunk, customer SIEM).

4) Severity matrix (proposal)
- Sev 1 (customer outage impacting production CUs): auto-escalate to on-call SRE + security lead. Target MTTR: 15 min. Requires 1 on-call approval + logging to immutable audit store.
- Sev 2 (degraded performance or partial routing issues): on-call SRE + product PM approval within 60 min. Requires logged approval, email/Slack thread ID captured.
- Sev 3 (informational/non-customer-visible): track in ticket; no immediate rollback; normal change process.

5) Proposed emergency approval flow (fast path)
- Trigger: Incident declared by customer or by Redwood monitoring (automated detection). Create Incident ID and link to ticket (INF-####) and PagerDuty incident.
- Step 1: Initial triage by on-call SRE. If triage suggests network rollback, SRE opens the "Emergency Network Rollback" workflow in Console (or a minimal CLI flag).
- Step 2: Rapid approval: require one SRE on-call approver + one customer-specified approver (if configured). If customer approver not reachable within severity window, fallback to Redwood Security Lead approval (escalation rule). All approvals include a short justification string.
- Step 3: Execute rollback via documented automation (Terraform destroy/apply reversal, or control-plane revert endpoint). Execution agent must produce: action id, before/after config snapshot, exit codes, stdout/stderr capture.
- Step 4: Post-action verification: automated smoke tests + customer ack. If rollback fails, escalate to War Room.

6) Audit logging requirements (schema and retention)
- Required fields for every recorded action: incident_id, action_id (uuid), actor (email), actor_role (SRE|Security|CustomerAdmin), approval_ids (list of approval uuids), approval_timestamps, justification_text, action_type (rollback|config-change|manual-intervention), target_resource (vpc-id, route-table-id, device-id), before_snapshot_url, after_snapshot_url, execution_output_url, sha256_of_snapshot, outcome (success|partial|failed), correlation_ids (ticket, PD, slack_thread).
- Immutable store: write logs to an append-only audit ledger (WORM) for at least 90 days by default; enterprise customers can request extended retention (configurable). Mirror to customer-provided logging endpoint if the customer has enabled log forwarding.
- Access model: RBAC — only SREs with incident role + security team can redact logs; redaction must itself be an auditable action.

7) Automation and tooling
- Console quick-action: Emergency Rollback button that collects necessary meta (incident, reason, target) and builds a rollback proposal. Must show who needs to approve and provide an ETA countdown.
- CLI fallback: redwood rollback --incident INF-2748 --target vpc-12345 --reason "route-change regression" --approver-email a.patel@redwood.ai (interactive OTP for approval).
- Execution agent: run in ephemeral, ephemeral-runner that writes snapshots to S3 with server-side encryption and pushes event record to audit ledger.

8) Customer-managed networking considerations
- When customer manages key network components, require a pre-agreed onboarding document that contains: list of customer approvers (names/emails), reachable escalation contacts, allowed rollback actions Redwood may take under emergency terms, and log-forwarding endpoints.
- If customer denies rollback (explicit opt-out), Redwood will provide a read-only recovery plan and recommended mitigations; legal/contract escalation path to be followed for critical SLO breaches.

9) Post-incident comms and postmortem
- After any emergency rollback, generate a postmortem with: timeline (from detection to resolution), artifacts (snapshots, approvals, logs), rollback rationale, and corrective actions. Postmortem must be published to Confluence and the customer (if they request it).
- Runbook item: within 24 hours, ensure all related audit logs are archived to the long-term retention bucket (if enterprise contract requires).

10) Example scenarios (concrete)
- Scenario A: Customer route table propogation breaks production traffic after a config push. On-call SRE detects and opens workflow. Customer approver takes 3 minutes to sign off via Console. Rollback executed automatically; success verified via health checks. Incident closed in 18 minutes.
- Scenario B: Customer has opted out of auto rollbacks. Customer network team must apply rollback; Redwood provides signed revert manifest and live support channel. Document steps to hand over artifacts and preserve audit trail.

11) Telemetry and SLOs to measure
- Time from incident open -> approval granted (target < 10 min for Sev1).
- Time from approval -> rollback executed (target < 5 min for automated flows).
- Percentage of rollbacks executed using automated tool vs manual interventions.
- Audit log ingestion latency to immutable store (target < 30s).

12) Security and privacy notes
- Do not log customer payloads or PII in snapshots; snapshots should be network config only and stripped of secrets (keys, tokens). If secrets are required for rollback, use KMS/HSM temporary access tokens and ensure they are never persisted in plaintext.
- All logs in the audit ledger must be encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys if requested (KMS integration).

13) Onboarding checklist (items to capture before we are allowed to perform auto-rollbacks)
- Signed emergency rollback permission in contract / BAA addendum if required.
- Customer approver contact list + 2 backup contacts + escalation windows.
- Log-forwarding destination (optional).
- Smoke tests / health checks defined and published for acceptance.
- Maximum allowed rollback actions enumerated (e.g., revert route table, disable peering, toggle NAT).

14) Open questions and next steps (team TODOs)
- Q1: Should we require two approvers (SRE + Customer) for all Sev1 rollbacks or allow SRE solo in first 10 minutes? Tradeoff: speed vs stronger audit.
- Q2: How do we present redaction requests from customers while maintaining an immutable audit trail?
- Q3: What is the legal surface if we perform a rollback that breaks a customer's internal compliance process? Need Legal input.
- Actions: prototype Console quick-action (ENG-PRIO), design audit-log schema in schema repo (APPLIED-ML linked), draft contract language with Legal and CS.

15) Appendix: Quick CLI examples (notes)
- redwood incident open --title "routing regression" --severity sev1 --target vpc-12345
- redwood rollback propose --incident INF-2748 --target route-table-rtb-22 --snapshots s3://audits/inf-2748-before.json
- redwood rollback approve --action 6f2f8e --approver a.patel@redwood.ai --justification "restore traffic"

Notes to reviewers: This doc mixes tactical runbook steps with product decisions — intended to be iterated quickly with SRE and Security. Remove/replace placeholders (INF-2748 ticket, sample S3 path) before marking final.

Unresolved: decide default audit retention (90d vs 365d) + account for e-discovery requests.

-- end of draft --
